newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Chase transfers $300 mln credit to Ecuador.
newsitem.headline: Chase transfers $300 mln credit to Ecuador.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp has transferred $300 million to Ecuador's central bank as part of the credit agreement to issue Eurobonds that was signed with the bank in December, a finance ministry official said Friday.
"The bank forwarded the $300 million as part of the credit agreement that will be financed through a Eurobond issue," an official at finance ministry told Reuters.
The source, who asked not to be named, said: "The credit was transferred directly to the central bank's foreign reserves that stood at $1.84 billion on Jan 17."
Chase Manhattan is leading a consortium of international banks that extended the credit to Ecuador and is preparing the launch of what will be Ecuador's Eurobonds.

According to the official the issue will be a five-year bond and is likely to be priced at 350 basis points over similar U.S. Treasury bonds. The official said there could still be changes to the issue, however. He said the issue is likely to be placed in coming days.
Ecuador has launched an ambitious economic program which includes a key policy of "Convertibility," a plan to peg the value of the sucre to the dollar in July.
